budget_items.topic: Mini-split heat pumps as a heat source
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said using mini-splits as a heat source, not just AC, was what enabled the project to qualify for free (grant) money. Getting the school administration to see the heating benefit, not just cooling, was described as a struggle.

budget_items.topic: Comparing mini-split cost to fossil fuel heating
budget_items.what_was_said: A member argued that when a building considers full electrification, the town should also be shown a traditional fossil-fuel cost comparison so voters can make an informed choice.

budget_items.topic: Geothermal wells at a school (state-pushed option)
budget_items.what_was_said: The state was said to be pushing geothermal; a school the size of the middle-high school reportedly drilled a large number of wells, and a member questioned what the return on investment would be.

A member said solar credits from Turkey Hill's panels are going somewhere and could fund the building's electricity so taxes don't rise as much, but the group has lost access to records of what the panels have actually saved since the installer went out of business.

The group discussed whether the town's ground-mount solar bylaw, which capped systems at a certain size, needs updating since panel efficiency has risen and the old cap now limits how much of a home's usage can be offset. They agreed it was worth looking into but did not resolve it.

budget_items.topic: Grant money vs. town-meeting funding requests
budget_items.what_was_said: A member described the task force's ongoing push to get the new town manager, select board, schools, and other town facilities to check with them for available grant/free money before putting funding requests on a town meeting warrant.

budget_items.topic: Next Green Communities grant round projects
budget_items.what_was_said: The task force said it is struggling to identify projects for the next spring grant round, after the mini-split project.

decisions.decision: Members agreed the town's ground-mount solar system size bylaw likely needs to be reviewed, without settling on a change.
